::: {.unit-header}
# 🌡️ Unit 4: Climate Change
**How do natural factors contribute to changes in Earth's temperature? What are 99.9% of climate scientists seeing in historical climate data that makes them so sure humans are the cause of climate change today, and why does it matter?**
:::

## Anchor Phenomenon

> **Earth's temperature is rising, reversing the cooling trend that occurred over the past 2,000 years, putting millions of people in harm's way, yet the public is not convinced of the risks.**
>
> Climate has changed in the past because of natural factors. Today's change is different: 99.9% of climate scientists agree that **humans are the cause**, which also means humans can take action to limit the changes and their consequences.

## Unit Driving Question

> **How do natural factors contribute to changes in Earth's temperature? What are 99.9% of climate scientists seeing in historical climate data that makes them so sure humans are the cause of climate change today, and why does it matter?**

**Performance task:** *Educating your community about the predicted impacts of climate change on human populations.* You will communicate the scientific consensus to someone in your community who is skeptical. To do so, you will:

1. **Analyze and interpret data** to confirm that human activities are causing climate change right now
2. **Analyze and interpret data** to determine future impacts of climate change
3. **Explain** how these impacts are expected to affect human populations

## Unit Storyline

| Lesson | Question |
|---|---|
| [Unit Opening](unit4-opening.qmd) | How do natural factors contribute to changes in Earth's temperature, and why are scientists so sure humans are the cause today? |
| [Seasons (Optional)](unit4-seasons-optional.qmd) | How does the annual cycle of the Earth around the Sun create seasonal temperature variations? |
| [Earth-Sun Dynamics](unit4-earth-sun-dynamics.qmd) | What factors have contributed to climate change in the past, and are they contributing to climate change now? |
| [Climate Feedbacks](unit4-climate-feedbacks.qmd) | What is causing global temperatures to rise, and why is the Arctic warming at almost 4 times the rate of the rest of the globe? |
| [The Past and the Future](unit4-past-and-future.qmd) | Have humans experienced dramatic climate change in the past? How were they impacted, and what does that tell us about the future? |
| [Unit Closing](unit4-closing.qmd) | What are scientists seeing in the data that makes them sure humans are the cause, and why does it matter to your community? |

## What You'll Figure Out

By the end of this unit, you will be able to:

::: {.key-idea}
- ☀️ **Explain** how Earth's tilt and its orbit around the Sun cause seasonal temperature changes
- 🌀 **Use** orbital cycle data (eccentricity, tilt, and precession) to explain glacial and interglacial periods
- 📉 **Show** that orbital cycles and solar output point to slow cooling today, so they cannot explain current warming
- 🏭 **Explain** how carbon dioxide from human activities strengthens the greenhouse effect
- 🧊 **Model** how feedbacks like ice-albedo make the Arctic warm almost 4 times faster than the rest of the globe
- 🌊 **Describe** how past climate changes, like the end of the last ice age and the Younger Dryas, affected human populations
- 🏙️ **Predict** how future climate change will affect people, including your own community
:::
